rules.statement: When concurrent callers request the same expensive remote resource, share a single in-flight retrieval (e.g. a ConcurrentDictionary of Lazy<Task<T>> keyed by the resource) instead of starting one per caller, and remove the in-flight entry when the retrieval ends.
rules.why: A burst of requests for one resource otherwise repeats the same download once per concurrent check.
rules.check: Look for a fetch-then-cache path where the cache miss path downloads directly, so concurrent misses each start their own HTTP request.

rules.statement: Run a retrieval shared by several callers with CancellationToken.None, bound it only by its own configured timeout, and have each caller wait on it with Task.WaitAsync(cancellationToken).
rules.why: One caller cancelling must not break the shared retrieval for the other callers.
rules.check: Look for a shared or coalesced task that is started with the first caller's cancellation token, or callers that await the shared task directly with no WaitAsync(cancellationToken).

rules.statement: Give a retrieval shared by several callers its own copies of the inputs it needs (for example, load a fresh X509Certificate2 from the raw data) instead of using objects that the first caller owns and may dispose.
rules.why: A caller that disposes its own objects, such as the certificates of its chain, must not break the retrieval for the others.
rules.check: Look for a shared background task that captures a caller-owned IDisposable (certificate, stream, chain) rather than a copy it owns.

rules.statement: Cache a failed remote retrieval (negative caching) for a configured duration, and don't retry the source while that entry exists, instead of paying the full fetch and timeout on every request or adding retry-with-backoff.
rules.why: Without it, an unreachable source costs a full timeout on every request. The remembered failure serves as the backoff.
rules.check: Look for a remote fetch whose failure path caches nothing, so each later request retries right away, or for added retry/backoff loops where a failure cache would do.

rules.statement: Expose network retrieval limits such as the fetch timeout, the maximum response size and cache durations as strictly bound options that are validated at host startup (timeout accepted by a timer, size at least one, durations above zero), not as constants in code.
rules.why: Fixed limits can't be tuned. A bad value should stop the host at startup, not fail on the first retrieval.
rules.check: Look for hard-coded TimeSpan or byte-size limits on HTTP fetches or caches, or for new options that have no startup validator.

rules.statement: Make a limit that governs a retrieval shared across tenants a host-wide option, not a per-tenant setting.
rules.why: One retrieval serves every tenant that names the same resource, so a per-tenant value has no single meaning.
rules.check: Look for timeouts or sizes of a shared fetch that are read from tenant or client settings.

rules.statement: Keep caches of large, rebuildable remote data and of per-replica fetch failures in process memory (IMemoryCache), not in the cross-replica shared-state store.
rules.why: Such data can be rebuilt from its source and can be large, and one replica's network failure must not stop the other replicas.
rules.check: Look for downloaded lists, documents or failure markers written to a distributed/shared-state cache.

rules.statement: Express a policy as one enumerated setting value (e.g. online, online_soft_fail, none), not as a separate boolean beside the mode setting.
rules.why: One policy setting states one policy. A boolean beside a mode creates meaningless combinations.
rules.check: Look for a new boolean flag that changes how an existing mode setting behaves, such as a soft-fail flag next to a 'none' mode.

rules.statement: Make certificate revocation checking fail closed by default: refuse an unknown status unless the tenant or client opts into soft-fail, and log a warning whenever soft-fail accepts a certificate with unknown status.
rules.why: A secure default fails closed. Soft-fail lets revoked certificates through when a list fails verification, is unavailable or is unsupported.
rules.check: Look for revocation code that treats unknown or unavailable status as valid by default, or that accepts it under soft-fail without logging a warning.

rules.statement: Have a revocation checker answer 'unknown', never 'good', for revocation sources or list forms it does not support (delta, partitioned or indirect CRLs, a CRL signed by another CA key) and for lists it cannot retrieve or verify.
rules.why: Only a verified list can show that a certificate is not revoked. Unsupported forms have to go through the fail-closed or soft-fail policy.
rules.check: Look for code paths that skip a CRL or extension they don't recognize and return not-revoked.

rules.statement: Accept an RSASSA-PSS signature (OID 1.2.840.113549.1.1.10) only with explicit parameters per RFC 4055: SHA-256/384/512 with absent or NULL hash parameters, MGF1 over the same hash, a salt length equal to the hash length, and a trailer field that is absent or 1. Refuse defaulted (SHA-1) parameters and SHA-1 signatures.
rules.why: Defaulted PSS parameters mean SHA-1, which must not be accepted.
rules.check: Look for PSS verification that uses default parameters, doesn't compare the MGF1 hash or salt length with the signature hash, or allows SHA-1.
